# Brings up ros2_control (mock GenericSystem, joints joint_a/joint_b) with
# joint_state_broadcaster and position_controller (ForwardCommandController).
# Long-running nodes are started in the background; the script returns once
# both controllers report "active".

DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash

mkdir -p "$DIR/log"

ROBOT_DESC="$(cat "$DIR/robot.urdf")"

nohup ros2 run robot_state_publisher robot_state_publisher \
  --ros-args -p robot_description:="$ROBOT_DESC" -p use_sim_time:=false \
  > "$DIR/log/robot_state_publisher.log" 2>&1 &
disown

nohup ros2 run controller_manager ros2_control_node \
  --ros-args --params-file "$DIR/controllers.yaml" \
  > "$DIR/log/ros2_control_node.log" 2>&1 &
disown

# spawner waits for the controller_manager services to come up, then loads,
# configures and activates both controllers before exiting.
ros2 run controller_manager spawner \
  joint_state_broadcaster position_controller \
  -c controller_manager --controller-manager-timeout 30 \
  > "$DIR/log/spawner.log" 2>&1

disown

# Brings up ros2_control (mock GenericSystem, joints joint_a/joint_b) with
# joint_state_broadcaster and position_controller (ForwardCommandController).
# Long-running nodes are started in the background; the script returns once
# both controllers report "active".

source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash

mkdir -p "$DIR/log"

  --ros-args -p robot_description:="$ROBOT_DESC" -p use_sim_time:=false \
  > "$DIR/log/robot_state_publisher.log" 2>&1 &
disown

nohup ros2 run controller_manager ros2_control_node \
  --ros-args --params-file "$DIR/controllers.yaml" \
  > "$DIR/log/ros2_control_node.log" 2>&1 &
disown

# configures and activates both controllers before exiting. This host's
# default ROS domain may have other controller_manager nodes on it, so a
# single attempt can occasionally race against the wrong one; retry until
# our own controllers actually report "active".
for i in $(seq 1 20); do
  ros2 run controller_manager spawner \
    joint_state_broadcaster position_controller \
    -c controller_manager --controller-manager-timeout 30 \
    >> "$DIR/log/spawner.log" 2>&1

     && ros2 control list_controllers 2>/dev/null | grep -q "^position_controller.*active"; then
    break
  fi
  sleep 1
done

done

# with joint_state_broadcaster and position_controller (ForwardCommandController).

# Avoid piling up duplicate instances from previous runs of this script.
pkill -f "$DIR/controllers.yaml" 2>/dev/null
pkill -f "ros2_control name=\"TwoJointSystem\"" 2>/dev/null
pkill -f "TwoJointSystem" 2>/dev/null
sleep 1

: > "$DIR/log/ros2_control_node.log"
: > "$DIR/log/spawner.log"

  --ros-args -p robot_description:="$ROBOT_DESC" -p use_sim_time:=false \
  > "$DIR/log/robot_state_publisher.log" 2>&1 &
disown

nohup ros2 run controller_manager ros2_control_node \
  --ros-args --params-file "$DIR/controllers.yaml" \
  > "$DIR/log/ros2_control_node.log" 2>&1 &
CM_WRAPPER_PID=$!
disown

# Give DDS discovery time to settle so our controller_manager is fully
# visible before the spawner's service calls go out.
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  grep -q "Resource Manager has been successfully initialized" "$DIR/log/ros2_control_node.log" 2>/dev/null && break
  sleep 0.5
done
sleep 2

# spawner loads, configures and activates both controllers. Verify success by
# reading THIS run's own controller_manager log (unambiguous), not the shared
# `ros2 control list_controllers` CLI, since a request on the default topic
# names can be answered by any controller_manager node on the domain.
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  ros2 run controller_manager spawner \
    joint_state_broadcaster position_controller \
    -c controller_manager --controller-manager-timeout 30 \
    >> "$DIR/log/spawner.log" 2>&1

  if grep -q "Activating controllers: \[ joint_state_broadcaster \]" "$DIR/log/ros2_control_node.log" 2>/dev/null \

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Brings up ros2_control (mock_components/GenericSystem, joints joint_a/joint_b)
# with joint_state_broadcaster and position_controller (ForwardCommandController).
# Long-running nodes are started in the background; the script returns once
# the controllers have been loaded, configured and activated.

DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash

mkdir -p "$DIR/log"

ROBOT_DESC="$(cat "$DIR/robot.urdf")"

nohup ros2 run robot_state_publisher robot_state_publisher \
  --ros-args -p robot_description:="$ROBOT_DESC" -p use_sim_time:=false \
  > "$DIR/log/robot_state_publisher.log" 2>&1 &
disown

nohup ros2 run controller_manager ros2_control_node \
  --ros-args --params-file "$DIR/controllers.yaml" \
  > "$DIR/log/ros2_control_node.log" 2>&1 &
disown

# spawner waits for the controller_manager services to come up, then loads,
# configures and activates both controllers before exiting.
ros2 run controller_manager spawner \
  joint_state_broadcaster position_controller \
  -c controller_manager --controller-manager-timeout 30 \
  > "$DIR/log/spawner.log" 2>&1
